narrative.overview:
The Companion Studio Poster makes ambitious engineering feel approachable. Warm paper, deep green-black ink and a vermilion disk frame an ivory chibi Kishu puppy; mint brings a quieter working surface into the same world. The Japanese influence comes through composition, the sun geometry and a small amount of Japanese lettering.

Large curved display type and generous editorial spacing give the identity room. Fine rules and compact, readable UI organize the denser technical material. The full-body puppy and compact stamp are the reusable identity: preserve their ivory fur, mint shading and vermilion bandana across light and dark applications.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and ink foundations, with vermilion identity accents and mint working surfaces.
Curved Bricolage display lettering, Geist interface copy and Geist Mono commands.
Editorial rules, modest rounded controls and selective soft depth.
One puppy identity expressed as a full character and a compact stamp.

rules.name: The Color Roles Rule
rules.body: Use ink for reading and primary actions, vermilion for identity and focus, and mint for working surfaces and the contrasting action on ink.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Bricolage carries headings and the wordmark; Geist carries explanations and controls; Geist Mono carries commands, code and technical status.

rules.name: The Resolved Cascade Rule
rules.body: Use the final, applicable CSS declaration when extending a component. The early compact media rules are not a second typography system.

rules.name: The Selective Lift Rule
rules.body: Keep editorial sections flat. Use soft depth for the walkthrough, its embedded preview, transient feedback and the isolated puppy artwork.

dos: Do keep the full puppy and compact stamp recognizable on paper, ink and vermilion backgrounds.
Do use the three font roles and preserve readable explanatory copy, generally 12–14px in compact content and larger for introductions.
Do retain visible vermilion keyboard focus and inline SVG icons with text or accessible labels.
Do stack the walkthrough at 800px and the principal page columns at 600px.
Do preserve reduced-motion behavior when adding transitions or mascot interactions.
donts: Don't replace the puppy identity with unrelated decorative symbols or generic stock imagery.
Don't turn the display face into the body or code face.
Don't promote superseded tiny declarations, decorative specimen captions or isolated density exceptions into reusable type roles.
Don't replace the soft shadows with hard offset shadows or apply raised cards to every editorial section.
Don't invent form-field styles from this page; it contains controls and copyable code, but no editable fields.
